decisions.reason: As a consumer-facing superfood product with weaker fit to the firm's core industrial waste-to-energy and engineering activities, it is the most likely option to be abandoned so resources can be redeployed to higher-synergy technologies.

These modular plant extensions fit the established business well and can be kept open as a relatively low-cost option that complements existing technical offerings despite limited visible evidence of breakout traction.

The waste-oil-to-energy plant was given its own page, a quantified launch message and flagship status, so management would likely continue backing it because uncertainty remains but the strategic upside is high.

The plastic-waste-to-fuel plant is close to the core offer and was elevated to flagship status, making it worth retaining as an option even though commercialization risk in this area is still substantial.
